implemented.note: The HMAC digest is framed inside the first application-data record (the earlier code wrote the 8 bytes before the record header, so the pinned server parsed them as a record length and never matched). The camouflage client also disables TLS 1.3 session tickets, so the read digest ends on the pinned server's current/previous write hash instead of including a ticket the server hashed later.

implemented.note: Salamander wraps every datagram and only QUIC long-header packets (first byte 0x80) are fragmented: 0x80 | msg id | (index << 4 | total) | pad length | pad | chunk, all inside a Salamander frame with its own salt. Replies are reassembled with the pinned TTL (8 s), per-source (8) and global (4096) caps. Verified end to end against the pinned hysteria2 listener with obfs: gecko, and at the socket layer for the long-header/short-header split.

implemented.note: The pinned hysteria2 listener does not share one QUIC transport across a multi-port listen list, so the pinned end-to-end case uses a single-port pool (selection path). implemented.note: quinn has no pacing hook; the Brutal window (bps * smoothed_rtt * 2 / ack_rate) is exposed through Controller::window, which is the pinned sender's send gate.

quinn's BBR has no upstream profile selector, so conservative/standard/aggressive map to 24/32/40 initial packets. The A2 build set the hysteria2 `cwnd` window unconditionally, which made the profile branch unreachable; the profile now takes precedence over `cwnd` in the BBR arm, and the pinned peer case exercises the profile without `up`/Brutal. Recorded as an approximation, not profile-gain parity.
The engine has no Hysteria2 UDP session relay, so the value is applied to the QUIC initial path MTU (the pinned default 1197 is 1200 - 3). The UDP session itself remains a named gap.

implementation: src/outbound/hysteria2_realm.rs (control HTTP/1.1 over TLS, STUN, punch, QUIC over the punched socket)
src/proxies.rs::parse_hysteria2_realm (control TLS identity and the pinned port-hop exclusion)
implemented.note: The client resolves the control URL, binds one UDP socket per family, discovers its mapped address with STUN binding requests (XOR-MAPPED-ADDRESS), posts /v1/{realm-id}/connect with the nonce/key, punches with HYRLMv1 HELLO/ACK packets (100 ms, 10 s cap, symmetric-NAT candidate expansion) and runs the QUIC handshake over the same socket to the returned peer address. The realm control TLS block now carries its identity: `fingerprint` is the pinned SHA-256 of the presented certificate DER and is installed before `skip-cert-verify`, so a pin is still enforced when the insecure flag is set (matching `ca.GetTLSConfig`); `certificate`/`private-key` are loaded and presented as the control mTLS client identity. Both are validated at load (inline PEM or an absolute path, both fields together), so an unsupported shape is a named rejection rather than a silent drop. `realm-opts` plus a non-empty `ports` pool is rejected with the pinned `realm and port hopping are mutually exclusive`. Verified end to end with the pinned `hysteria2-realm` control listener plus a pinned `hysteria2` listener with `realm-opts` registering to it; both sides use a loopback STUN server, so the control HTTP, STUN, punch and post-punch QUIC connection are all exercised. The control client speaks HTTP/1.1 (control servers also serve h2, which this path does not negotiate).
